institution: Sir Ganga Ram Hospital, New Delhi
citation: Department of Clinical Microbiology and Immunology, Sir Ganga Ram Hospital. Clinical Microbiology Newsletter, Vol. 22, No. 1: percentage sensitivity, January to December 2015. New Delhi: Sir Ganga Ram Hospital; published June 2016.
reporting: Percent susceptible by specimen (blood, urine, pus wound swab, body fluids, respiratory isolates), organism (Gram-positive and Gram-negative tables) and location (OPD, ward, ICU), with the number of isolates per row; organism counts per specimen and location in bar charts with printed data labels and an "others" list.
method: MIC testing on Vitek 2, interpreted with CLSI 2014 guidelines (as the table note line states for these 2015 data); repeat isolates excluded (printed in parentheses).

verification.note: All 10 susceptibility tables (GPC and GNB, pages 2 to 6) were parsed from the PDF text layer (sgrhgrid2.py: pdfplumber word positions; column headers rebuilt from the rotated header text; OPD, ward and ICU taken from each row's background colour and checked against the row order; organism labels assigned to each triple of rows by vertical position), then every cell and every row n was compared by eye with the pages rendered at scale 4 and cropped into left and right halves: no differences; the cells the validator does not keep were re-read (the three caution cells again at scale 6). Organism bar charts: bar data labels were matched to the legend by legend order and swatch colour (barcounts.py) and the "others" lists parsed from the text layer inside each panel's box; every panel was checked arithmetically (legend counts plus Others equal the printed Isolates, the "others" list sums to Others, the bar values equal the text-layer data labels) and every panel was compared by eye with the chart rendered at scale 3.2; every recorded row n equals its chart count. The body fluid OPD and ICU legends were read from the image because the bar parse found no bars there (E. coli 24, Staphylococci spp. 13, Enterococci spp. 12, Others 46; Klebseilla spp. 21, E. coli 21, Enterococci spp. 16, Others 35); both balance and match the text-layer labels and the table n. Second reader 2026-09-26: see issues.

notes: Clinical Microbiology Newsletter of Sir Ganga Ram Hospital, Volume 22, No. 1 (published June 2016), data January to December 2015, 8 pages; the bar-chart layout used in the 2024 file. Pages 2 to 6 give one specimen each (blood; urine; pus wound swab; body fluids; respiratory isolates): organism bar charts for OPD, ward and ICU (samples, positives, isolates, bars with printed data labels and a colour legend, and an "others" list) and Gram-positive (GPC) and Gram-negative (GNB) percentage sensitivity tables with three rows per organism (OPD, ward, ICU, by the colour key) and the number of isolates; "-" means not done. Specimens recorded as blood, urine, pus (printed "Pus wound swab"), sterile (printed "Body fluids") and respiratory (printed "Respiratory isolates"). Rows printed "Staphylococci spp." are separate from Staph. aureus and are recorded as coagulase-negative staphylococci, as the 2011 edition labels the same row "Staphylococci spp. (CONS)"; enterococci ("Enterococci spp.", urine "Enterococcus spp."), Klebsiella and Acinetobacter are reported at genus level. Combined columns: "Cefoxitin / Oxacillin" (blood, body fluid and respiratory GPC tables; the urine and pus GPC tables print "Oxacillin" alone, recorded without a combined-column note) is recorded under oxacillin, "Imipenem / Meropenem" (every GNB table) under meropenem, and "Glycopeptide" (body fluids: "Glycopeptides") under vancomycin; each such cell says so in its note. The "Quinolones" column (no agent named) is not recorded; blood Salmonella also print nalidixic acid and chloramphenicol (recorded). The table note line on every page reads "according to 2014 CLSI guidelines" although the data are for 2015; recorded as CLSI 2014. Colistin and tigecycline are printed as percent susceptible for Enterobacterales and non-fermenters; no interpretive criteria are stated for them beyond that note line. Isolate numbers: every recorded row n equals its organism's chart count (legend bar or "others" entry); there are no chart and table mismatches. Three Imipenem/Meropenem percentages cannot be produced by the row's n (urine ICU Enterobacter n=4, 40; urine ICU Acinetobacter n=5, 14; pus ICU Acinetobacter n=14, 6): per-drug tested numbers are not printed; recorded as printed, with a conflict note on each cell. The blood OPD and ward chart panels print the same "Samples 4782" and the same repeat figures (132) and (142); sample figures are not recorded. Organism counts: every legend and "others" entry whose organism has a canonical key is recorded, with misspellings and variants mapped to the intended organism ("Klebseilla spp." as Klebsiella spp., "Serratia marscecens", "Morganii spp." as Morganella, "E. meningoseptica" as Elizabethkingia meningoseptica, "S. maltophila", "S. paucimobilis", "Strept. viridans" as viridans group streptococci, "L.monocytogenes", "Staphylococci spp." as coagulase-negative staphylococci, "Enterococci spp." as Enterococcus spp.); entries without a key, or that would add to the key of a tabulated organism, are listed in excluded. The respiratory ward "others" list prints both "S. maltophilia-7" and "S. maltophila-1"; both entries are recorded as printed (the build adds counts of the same organism). "S. pyogenes Group A" is recorded as Streptococcus pyogenes (the 2015 tables have no S. pyogenes rows). Fungal isolates are counted in the charts; their susceptibility data were to be published separately in the next issue. Page 1 (Brucella vertebral osteomyelitis case report and SGRH brucellosis data 2012 to 2015), page 7 (prescription auditing of antimicrobials and drug resistance index trends) and page 8 (case report continued, conferences and workshops, publications, highlights based on blood isolates in IPD, faculty) are not susceptibility tables. The PDF has no direct link: sgrh.com serves it only by an HTTP POST from the Microbiology Newsletter selector on https://sgrh.com/en/publications (issue "June-2016"; the server names the file mb-june2016.pdf); the downloaded file opens completely (8 pages).
issues: Second reader 2026-09-26: all 1,126 cells, all 108 row n values and all 260 organism counts checked against the PDF: the seeded 25% sample of 282 cells from sample_cells.py (drawn from all 10 GPC and GNB tables on pages 2 to 6) was read blind from the page images (tables at scale 3 cut into halves with the row labels and n kept; small tables at scale 2 to 3) before comparing with the extraction, and every cell, every row n, every row's fill colour and every row label was also compared with an independent parse of the text layer written for this check (cell rectangles by fill colour, values centred in each cell, rotated header text per column, labels by vertical position).

Result: 0 transcription errors, nothing corrected (sample 0 of 282; whole file 0 of 1,126 cells, 0 of 108 n, 0 of 260 counts). OPD, ward and ICU correct on every row (yellow, blue and pink row fills, the same as the colour key on each page, always in OPD, ward, ICU order); the organism label of every row triple is correct; every printed value of a recorded column is in the file; the 6 printed rows not recorded are exactly the 6 rows printed all "-", as excluded says. No table reached the 2% threshold.

Column headers: Cefoxitin / Oxacillin (blood, body fluid and respiratory GPC, 12 cells) and Oxacillin alone (urine and pus GPC, 8 cells) under oxacillin, Glycopeptide and Glycopeptides (38 cells) under vancomycin, Imipenem / Meropenem (66 cells) under meropenem and High Dose Gentamicin (9 cells) under gentamicin_hl match the printed headers of each table, and every combined-column cell carries its note; the body fluid GNB table has no Ceftazidime column; Quinolones is not recorded (excluded).

Charts: all 15 panels re-read from the images and the text layer. Every bar label, legend entry and "others" entry agrees with counts or excluded; every panel balances (legend counts plus Others equal Isolates, the "others" list sums to Others); bars pair with legend entries in column order and every bar's fill equals its swatch (the teal shared by Staphylococci spp. and Enterococci spp. is resolved by legend order and agrees with the table n); every row n equals its chart count.

Cells not kept: the 3 caution cells (urine ICU Enterobacter n=4 Imipenem/Meropenem 40; urine ICU Acinetobacter n=5, 14; pus ICU Acinetobacter n=14, 6) and the 45 intrinsic cells (Klebsiella and Enterobacter ampicillin, Acinetobacter aztreonam and nitrofurantoin, Proteus nitrofurantoin and colistin, P. aeruginosa co-trimoxazole) are printed that way, not transcription errors. The note line on pages 2 to 6 reads "according to 2014 CLSI guidelines" (confirmed on every page), so CLSI 2014 is as printed; this edition has no asterisk footnotes; the page 7 and page 8 figures quoted in excluded match the pages.
